summary: The contracts preserve PRD scope and provide coherent execution/security/recovery boundaries, but two current-source contradictions block implementation readiness: the UX contract still describes the approved design system as an empty scaffold, and the permission card contract lacks explicit mappings for unknown, transmission failure, expiry and cancellation to backend states/actions.

open_findings.finding: docs/design/specs/workbench-ux.md describes docs/design/system.md as an empty scaffold and says tokens, font, breakpoint and motion are undecided, while the current design system defines an authoritative token/component source, 163 tokens, 44 variants, typography, responsive widths and motion.
open_findings.required_change: Reconcile the UX contract and decision record with the current design system; distinguish existing six component families from remaining product-specific UI contracts and identify only genuinely open design work.

open_findings.finding: PermissionRequest maps pending/sending/approved/denied/stale only. It does not specify backend-to-UI mappings for decision_sending failure/unknown, expired, or cancelled; approved is not explicitly bound to confirmed applied evidence; user refusal and policy denial are not distinguished.
open_findings.required_change: Add explicit backend-to-component state/action mapping: approved only from confirmed applied receipt; sent/accepted distinct from applied; unknown and transport failure require reconciliation; expiry/cancellation distinct from refusal/policy deny; disable retry until fresh pending/revision state allows it.

provenance.routing_basis: coordinator-selected under standing user preference for independent design review
